issue: Visual-semantic ambiguity from annotation leader lines converging on / crossing the canonical dotted vertical line, plus overall annotation density. The thin red leader that connects the left-side 'break-even ≈ 7.5M / sensitivity ≈ 6.2–10.4M (a region, not a point)' box to the crossover star (at ~7.5M req/mo, right of the dotted line) must cross the vertical dotted 'canonical 6.24M req/mo' line to reach its target. At that same dotted line the green leader from the 'cloud $87.6K/mo (occupancy input)' box also terminates (on the cloud diamond), and the blue 'canonical 6.24M req/mo' label sits just above it. The result is a busy vertical where two leaders cross/meet and a label hangs, so a reader scanning quickly can mis-associate the red break-even box with the canonical 6.24M marker rather than with the 7.5M star. The numeric content itself is consistent (self-host $155,816.93/mo; managed $0.0208/req ⇒ 7.5M; band $0.015–0.025/req ⇒ 6.2–10.4M; cloud $87.6K at 6.24M; feasible max 40 rps × 624,000 s = 24.96M), so this is a layout/reading-order defect, not an arithmetic one.
evidence: Rendered page 294: red box at left (~y 3–5e5) with a single thin red leader running down-right to the star on the blue line at x≈7.5e6; that leader intersects the dotted vertical at x=6.24e6. Green box at left (~y 1e5) with a green leader ending on the diamond that lies on the same dotted vertical. Blue 'canonical 6.24M req/mo' text positioned directly above that dotted vertical. Three annotation elements therefore stack on one vertical line.
acceptance_test: Reposition the break-even box (or reroute its leader) so the red leader does not cross the canonical dotted line, and/or add an explicit arrowhead that lands unambiguously on the 7.5M star; verify at 150 dpi that (a) no leader crosses the dotted vertical, (b) each box's eye-path to its target is unambiguous, and (c) the canonical 6.24M label, the cloud diamond, and the break-even star are visually separable. If the box must stay left, consider a horizontal-then-vertical elbow that clears the dotted line.
